judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The span is the text of the breadcrumb link "Início" (13px, weight 600, so not large text) in the page-title band. Its colour #3399e7 is the breadcrumb link colour the live post-31589.css sets (--e-global-color-accent), and the band behind it is the primary-to-secondary linear-gradient background image. Sampling the screenshot gives #3399e7 on about #25689f, 1.92:1, matching the claimed 1.93:1 at best, well below the 4.5:1 that 1.4.3 requires. The live HTML and CSS give the same colours and gradient, and the screenshot is fully styled, so the capture matches what users get. The claim names the real failure.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The input is the email field of the footer newsletter sign-up form ("Cadastro"). It asks for the user's own email address, and email is one of the input purposes listed in WCAG 2.1 section 7. In the capture and in the live HTML it has type="email" and a screen-reader label "Email", but no autocomplete attribute. type="email" gives the data type, not the input purpose, and the sufficient technique H98 needs autocomplete="email". Without it the purpose is not programmatically determinable, so 1.3.5 fails, as the claim says. The live markup is identical.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The image is the ABN seal (owl, the name "Academia Brasileira de Neurologia" around the edge, "MCMLXII") at the top of the first footer column. It is not a link and has alt="" in both the capture and the live HTML. The claim holds of the capture: the image is hidden, and the text next to it (social links, contact details) does not give the organisation's name or the year. In my reading it does not fail 1.1.1. In this spot the seal is branding: the same footer ends with "© Academia Brasileira de Neurologia", and the page title and article name the organisation, so a null alternative loses only the founding year drawn into the seal. Many auditors, though, treat a logo as informative and want its alternative to give the organisation's name, so competent auditors would reasonably disagree. Label uncertain. (Separately, the header logo link wraps an image with alt="" and has no accessible name, a 2.4.4/4.1.2 problem on another element.)
